journal: Opened three positions on a clean risk-on read: SPY and QQQ both confirmed uptrend across 1d/5d/20d and above all three SMAs, sized near the 25% cap each (22.5% and 21.4% at cost). XLV was the one watchlist name showing short-term weakness (-0.82% 1d, -1.77% 5d) inside a longer uptrend (+5.23% 20d) -- bought a small starter clip (11.3%) on the pullback as a deliberate lower-conviction rotation candidate; if it keeps sliding this is my planned wash-sale test case for the week: sell it at a loss, then rebuy once trend confirms, and see whether the tax page tells me what that costs. Left 44.6% in cash, wanted room to add or to fund the wash-sale rebuy without touching unsettled proceeds. Fills all landed a few cents worse than the reference open, consistent with the documented 5bp adverse slippage. The macro page could not be used for the regime read as specified -- it always shows the live snapshot (dated Aug 14) rather than anything scoped to the session date (Jul 13), so I fell back to the watchlist's own SMA structure for risk-on/risk-off, which is point-in-time correct per the brief. Ticker search (native-setter input + submit dispatch) worked cleanly for XLE; the persona-spec workaround was not needed as a workaround, it just worked.

QQQ's session-1 invalidation (close below the 50-day SMA) fired on the 2026-07-13 close (711.74 vs stop 715.16), so I exited the full position. The overnight gap worked against the stop-loss logic in a good way this time: the session-2 open (720.22) was actually above my 718.08 entry, so the exit realized a small gain (+.34 gross before the /usr/bin/bash.06 SEC/TAF fee), not the loss I was bracing for -- worth remembering that a D-1 close trigger does not guarantee a loss at the D open fill. Recycled part of the freed conviction into XLE on a two-session momentum reversal (+3.01% 1d, +6.79% 5d, reclaiming its 20-day SMA), sized as tactical (21.7% at cost) given it is still below its 50-day SMA. XLV is now the one position underwater (-9.32 unrealized on the book as of today's close) -- watching it as my wash-sale candidate: if it stays negative I will realize the loss this week and rebuy once the dip-buy thesis either confirms or I want to re-test the tooling's wash-sale disclosure on a real loss-then-repurchase pair.

Cut XLV early on continued technical deterioration rather than waiting for the exact stop level -- realized a loss (proceeds 1101.10 vs cost basis 1127.35, roughly -26.25 gross before the 0.03 fee). This was deliberate: XLV was already my lowest-conviction position and I want to see how the tooling handles a loss-then-repurchase inside 30 days, so I plan to re-enter XLV in session 4 or 5 and check what the tax page and any wash-sale panel say about the disallowed amount, the basis rollover, and the earliest safe repurchase date. No new buy this session -- staying in cash while I decide the re-entry timing and level for XLV, and watching whether QQQ (still below its 20-day SMA but improving) sets up a clean second re-entry too.

Repurchased XLV one session after realizing the loss -- 7 shares at 160.43, inside 30 days of the 2026-07-15 loss sale, deliberately to trigger a wash sale and see what the tax page says about it: the disallowed amount, the basis it rolls into, the tolled holding period, and the earliest safe-to-repurchase date afterward. XLV held its 20-day SMA through the pullback, which is the technical case for re-entering at all; the timing relative to the prior loss sale is the point of the trade. No other changes this session -- SPY and XLE both still confirming their trends.

Final session: held the book unchanged. QQQ, which I exited session 2, is now decisively bearish (close 705.94, -3.28% 20d, below its 20/50-day SMAs) -- glad I did not chase a re-entry there. XLV and XLE both confirming (XLV +2.22% 1d/+5.79% 20d, XLE +0.92% 1d/+4.01% 5d), SPY flat. Closing the week at roughly 56% invested / 44% cash across SPY (39.8% of invested), XLE (40.2%), XLV (20.0%), none of which are near the 25% single-name cap since that cap is measured against total equity, not invested value. Confirmed the portfolio statement export (GET /api/portfolio/statement.md) renders cleanly with the wash-sale-adjusted XLV cost basis (1149.26) carried through, and the raw /api/portfolio JSON's money fields are clean decimal strings with no binary-float noise. Wrapping the week here.
